questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an east-flowing river of Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandavi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **East Flowing River of Karnataka**__
 
• __**Tungabhadra River**__
 __
 
• It is a sacred river in southern India that **flows through the state of Karnataka to Andhra Pradesh.** 
 
• The ancient name of the river was **Pampa**.
 
• The river is approximately 710 km long, and it drains an area of 72,200 sq km.
 
• It is** formed by the confluence of two rivers, the Tunga River and the Bhadra River.** 
 
• Both Tunga & Bhadra Rivers originate on the eastern slopes of the **Western Ghats**.
 
• The greater part of the Tungabhadra’s course **lies in the southern part of the Deccan plateau.** 
 
• The river is fed mainly by rain, and it has a monsoonal regimen with summer high water.
 
• Its **major tributaries** are the** Bhadra**, the **Haridra**, the **Vedavati**, the **Tunga**, the **Varda,** and the **Kumdavathi**.
 
• **It flows in a more or less northwest direction before joining the eastern river, Krishna. The Krishna River finally ends in the Bay of Bengal. Hence, It is the east-flowing river.**
 
 
 
• **Bhima river**__
 __
 
• It is also known as the **Chandra Bhaga** river.
 
• Bhima is the **longest** (largest is Tungabhadra) tributary of the river **Krishna**.
 
• It originates in the **Bhimashankar hills** in the Pune district of Maharashtra.
 
• Bhima river flows for a length of 861 km through the states of **Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana**, and then merges into river Krishna at Raichur in Karnataka. Hence, It is the east-flowing river.
 
• Bhima river has many tributaries such as **Ghod, Sina, Awarja, Kagna, Nira, Mon,** etc.
 
 
 
• **Manjira river**__
 __
 
• Length(KM): 724
 
• Catchment Area(sq km): 30844
 
• Originates in the **Balaghat Range** -Bhir district of Maharashtra
 
• **It flows in an east and south-easterly direction for about 512 km through the Osmanabad district -of Maharashtra, Bidar district of Mysore and Medak district of Andhra Pradesh before changing its direction Northwards near Sanga Reddipet. **Hence, It is the east-flowing river.
 
• After flowing for about 75 km further, the Manjira river enters the Nizamabad district of Andhra Pradesh and it also **forms the boundary between Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• **Mahadayi or Mhadei**__
 
 
• It is the **west-flowing river, that originates in Bhimgad Wildlife Sanctuary (Western Ghats)**, Belagavi district of **Karnataka**. Hence, It is a west-flowing river. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• It is essentially a **rain-fed river** also called **Mandovi **in Goa.
 
• It is joined by a number of streams to form the Mandovi which is one of two major rivers (the other one is the Zuari river) that flows through Goa.
 
• The river travels 35 km in Karnataka; 82 km in Goa before joining the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: In the context of climate, what is the full form of ITCZ?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Intertropical Convergence Zone, or ITCZ, is **the region that circles the Earth, near the equator.**
 
• Here the trade winds of the Northern and Southern hemispheres come together.
 
• The intense sun and warm water of the equator heats the air in the ITCZ, raising its humidity and making it buoyant.
 
• With the help of convergence of the trade winds, the buoyant air rises.
 
• As the air rises it expands and cools, releasing the accumulated moisture in an almost perpetual series of thunderstorms.

questions.question: Which layer of atmosphere can experience burning up of meteorites?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is like a blanket of air and consists of different gases like **Nitrogen-78 %, Oxygen-21 %, Argon-0.93 %, and Carbon dioxide-0.04 %.**
 
• ​Earth's atmosphere is composed of six layers and the mesosphere is one such layer-
 
• Mesosphere: 
 
 
• This layer lies above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere and extends from 50 to 80 km above the earth's surface.
 
• It is the middle layer of the atmosphere. Because of the thin air, you would not breathe easily in this layer. 
 
• Most of the meteors and rock are burned up in these layers before reaching the earth. 
 
• This layer has more gases than the above layers i.e. exosphere and thermosphere which causes more friction and heat to burn up meteors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**Other layers are as follows: **

 
• Troposphere: The troposphere is the innermost layer of the earth's atmosphere.

 
 
• Mixing up of gases and changing weather occurs in this layer.
 
• This layer is dense and closest to the earth's surface and 10 - 15 km above the surface.
 
• This layer consists of dense air, water vapour, the formation of clouds, and all-weather phenomena that take place in this layer. 
 
• Thus, this layer contains about 80% of the total mass of the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• Stratosphere: This layer lies above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
 
• The Earth's ozone layer is found in this layer.
 
• This ozone layer is located between 15 to 50 km above the surface.
 
• This layer absorbs the ultraviolet rays from the sun and gives protection to the earth from its harmful effects.
 
 
 
• Ionosphere: The Ionosphere is a highly active layer of the atmosphere as it shrinks or expands continuously depending upon the amount of energy absorbed.
 
 
• The sun radiation causes gases to form ions having an electric charge.
 
• This layer helps in propagating radio signals and sending them back to earth.
 
 
 
• Thermosphere: The thermosphere is located in between the exosphere and mesosphere.
 
 
• 'Thermos' means heat, this layer contains the most heat and this layer can produce heat up to 4,500 degrees Fahrenheit.
 
• This layer is the most thicker than all the inner layers of the atmosphere. 
 
 Exosphere: This is the outermost and thinner layer of the earth's atmosphere.

 
 
• It has a low atmospheric pressure and gas molecules are in wide spaces.
 
• It is composed of lighter gases like helium, argon, and hydrogen.

questions.question: How much water carried by the Indus river system can India use under the Indus water treaty (1960)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Indus water treaty (1960)**

 
 
• **​**The Indus Water Treaty is a water-distribution treaty **signed between India and Pakistan on 19 September 1960**.
 
• The treaty was signed by then **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and the President of Pakistan, Ayub Khan**.
 
• It was brokered by the **World Bank**.
 
• The treaty gives **India 20%** of the water from the Indus river system and the rest **80% to Pakistan**.
 
• Treaty gives India control over **3 eastern rivers (Beas, Ravi and Sutlej).**
 
• Pakistan gets control of **3 western rivers (Chenab, Indus and Jhelum)**.
 
• The treaty allows India to use the waters of the western rivers for **limited irrigation use** and **non-consumable use** for applications like **power generation, navigation etc.**

questions.question: After full moon day, every night the size of the bright part of the moon appears to become thinner and thinner. On the fifteenth day, the moon is not visible. This day is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** new moon day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **New Moon**__

 __
 
• When the sunlit portion is 0%, **it is termed a New Moon. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• After the full moon, the next fourteen days when the moon grows thinner and thinner and becomes invisible is called the waning phase of the moon.
 
• The sunlit portion of the Moon that can be viewed from the Earth, is termed the Phase of the Moon or the Lunar phases.
 
• The phases keep changing gradually over a period of 29.53 days (approx.).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **When the sunlit portion is 100%**, it is termed a Full Moon.
 
• **When the shape of the Moon is thinning from Full Moon to New Moon**, it is termed Waning.
 
• **When the shape of the Moon is thickening from the New Moon to Full Moon**, it is termed Waxing.

questions.question: Above which layer of the atmosphere does the Exosphere lies?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Thermosphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The exosphere **is the outermost layer of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It starts at an altitude of about 500 km and goes out to about 10,000 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The column of the atmosphere is divided into five different layers depending upon the temperature condition.
 
• They are the** troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, and exosphere.**
 
• The** troposphere **is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere. Its average height is 13 km and extends roughly to a height of 8 km near

 the poles and about 18 km at the equator.
 
• The zone separating the troposphere from the stratosphere is known as the **tropopause.**
 
• The **stratosphere **is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• It contains the ozone layer.
 
• The** mesosphere** lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• The ionosphere is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• The** thermosphere** is known as the exosphere.
 
• This is the highest layer but very little is known about it.
